To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified a GAP that is specific for the CDC42GAPs, which includes CDC42Hs.

we have identified a human platelet GAP for the CDC42 Hs GTP-binding protein, and that this CDC42Hs GAP has a molecular weight of approximately 25 kDa, is a specific GAP for the CDC42 family of proteins, is capable of weakly stimulating the GTPase of the rho GTP-binding protein and, unlike ras- and rap-GAPs, does not stimulate the intrinsic GTPase activities for the ras or rap proteins.

the CDC42-GTP-activating protein has been purified and characterized from human platelets and that this protein is capable of stimulating the intrinsic GTPase activities (and thus, presumably, inactivating) of CDC42Hs and rho GTP-binding proteins.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of a GAP for the human platelet CDC44Hs protein.
the molecular mechanisms that regulate cell growth, differentiation, and cell motility.
identifying and characterizing a human platelet G-protein which may be involved in platelet activation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CDC42-GAP is a GAP for the GTPases CDC42Hs and rho, but not for ras or rap.
CDC42Hs is a member of the ras-related family of proteins which has a GAP activity that appears to be specific for this protein.
the CDC42GAP activity is a novel member of the ras-related family of GTP-binding protein-activating proteins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CDC42GAP is a specific and potent GAP for CDC42Hsc and that the CDC42Sc and CDC42Hs genes may have arisen from a common ancestor.
we have identified and purified from human platelets a GAP that is capable of selectively stimulating the intrinsic GTPase activities for the CDC42GAP and the CDC42Hsc GTP-binding proteins.
the CDC42GAP protein is an apparent human isoform of the GTP-binding protein, G25K, which is a member of the ras-related family of proteins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CDC42-GAP appears to have a specific role in modulating the GTPase cycle of CDC42Hs.
the CDC42GAP appears to be a GAP specific for CDC42Hsc, which is the human homolog of CDC42Sc, a protein which has been implicated in yeast cell-division-cycle control.
CDC42Hs is a GTP-binding protein which is capable of being stimulated by a specific GTPase- activating protein.
